data.name: CITYCONOMY: Service for your City
data.detailed_description:
Time to clean up!


Assume the many jobs of a service company and take care of a vibrant metropolis in the open-world city economy simulation CITYCONOMY. For you, that means: From the classic trash collection to drain cleaning, from towing services to lawn mowing, there's a wide range of missions available across the entire city! A total of 15 vehicles await you, even in multiplayer!

Explore a huge, open-world city with its various districts, such as the old town, industrial park and residential neighborhood. You'll find new tasks for your constantly growing fleet all over the city. If the residents are sat-isfied with you, you'll gain access to new skills, jobs and machines.



Complete realistic jobs in the field of city economy, such as towing cars, cleaning drains, improving roads and trimming hedges, all together with your friends in multiplayer mode. Complete the tasks and ensure that the city's residents are happy and satisfied. Build a company that generates profits and is a pillar of the local economy.

Up to 5 players can take part in multiplayer matches. The player who starts the game acts as the host. Complete a diverse spectrum of jobs together with your friends, or simply have fun in the open world.

What are you waiting for? Get behind the wheel of faithfully recreated vehicles from MAN and start the engine!

Featues:


  • Authentic simulation of municipal services such as trash collection, car towing, sewage and gardening
  • Open-world city with an industrial park, commercial center, suburbs, old town and residential district
  • Realistic weather system
  • Day and night cycle
  • Cooperative multiplayer mode for up to five players, including voice chat
  • Faithfully recreated vehicle models from MAN's current TGL and TGM series
  • Varied, dynamic job system, side quests, experience tree and man-agement section

reviews.review:
[h1]I thought of a new medical condition – simulator addict[/h1]

When you torture yourself and play even the most ridiculous and broken simulators that should be considered as medical condition. But what we can do? There’s not a lot to choose from.

Cityconomy is a simulator where to take care of the city. You collect garbage, clean the streets, do plumbing jobs and such.
It could be a fun game for simulator fans. The gameplay itself wouldn’t be mediocre if not for the repetitive tasks. I know all the simulators are repetitive, but that repetitiveness doesn’t get boring only if it’s a true simulator and really tries to be realistic. Because in that case every task, even if it’s the same task could be different and challenging. 

The career mode is quite long, there’s a lot to do and career progression is nicely made but it suffers from a lack of variety. You do your job and get paid...for hundreds of times Then you can expand your company, hire more drivers and buy more vehicles. I know it might seem boring for 99,99% of people but we simulator addicts are into this.

Sadly this is where all the good things end(or should I say best things this game has, they rather mediocre). Graphically the game looks horrible…no wait, horrible is the wrong word. Mobile games look better than this. It looks like abomination. And you know what’s the “best” part? It runs worse than GTAV, AC origins, FFXV and other very demanding games on max graphics. The performance is abysmal.
Maybe vehicle models could pass for decent looking, but everything else…the draw distance is maybe 100 meters. You think OMSI 2 looks bad? Think again, you haven’t seen this one. The city is absolutely dead, there are only few people and cars on the streets.
There are some graphical bugs, sky might disappear if you turn on shadows. And another ridiculous thing, on 14:15 it could start raining, 14:20 it’s sunny again, after 5 more minutes it’s raining again. 

Oh i almost forgot the most positive thing about this game. Physics are surprisingly good for such a game. I’m not saying it’s great, but vehicles have a weight to them and you can't just fly thought the streets. I really loves the handling.

If you ran out of simulators to play or want something different it may be worth buying at a very low price, like 2-5€. But that’s the only case when you should buy this. For others you probably want to stay away.
There is another game published by Stragon - Construction simulator, which suffers from similar problems but is much better. I respect Astragon, they're trying at least. so check out that game instead.


[b]Pros:[/b]
[list]
[*]Nice idea but poorly executed
[*]Decent physics
[/list]
[b]Cons:[/b]
[list]
[*]Graphics is a joke
[*]Performance…wtf?
[*]Gameplay is way too repetitive
[*]Bugs&glitches
[/list]
